file.content:
city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits;
            the result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The stored and
            returned value is that E.164 string, e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes
            '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation"
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2024-01-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag used on create. When an existing owner already has
            the same last name and the same address (compared case-insensitively
            with collapsed whitespace), the create is rejected with 409 unless
            this flag is set to true, which acknowledges the two owners share a
            household and allows the create to proceed.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          default: false
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.

The full build is green. 

## Summary

The spec required validating the E.164 telephone's national-number length against its country code (`+61` → 9 national digits, `+1` → 10), rejecting with 400 when wrong.

The validation flows through `@TelephoneValidation` on the owner DTO → `TelephoneValidator` → `E164Telephone.isValid`/`normalize`. I made the change in the one place that matters:

**`E164Telephone.java`** — after the existing 8–15 total-digit check, I added a per-country national-length rule driven by a small table:
- `"61"` → national number must be exactly 9 digits
- `"1"` → national number must be exactly 10 digits

The country code is matched against the leading digits of the E.164 form (ordered longest-prefix-first, unambiguous since `61` and `1` don't overlap). If a known country code matches, the national length (`digits.length() - countryCode.length()`) must equal the required value or `normalize` returns `null` (→ invalid → 400). Unknown country codes keep the existing general 8–15 behavior, so nothing else regresses. The normalization stays idempotent, and the default-AU path (`0412345678` → drop `0` → `+61412345678`, 9 national digits) still validates.

I also updated the `@TelephoneValidation` default message to describe the new rule.

Tests: `AcceptanceTest.errorRejectsWrongNationalLength` (`+61 123`) passes, and the full suite is **BUILD SUCCESS** (1 test, 0 failures).

Note: this is not a git repository, so there's nothing to commit.
